title: docs: publish the M17 security-boundary analysis, and gate named milestone deliverables
body:
## What this is

Phase 0 of this workstream was an independent audit of #36 (before touching anything); Phase 1–5 is
the **analysis half of `M17`** and the check that was missing when its deliverable was.

`M17` — "Security and authenticity boundary" — names exactly one deliverable in
`docs/architecture/roadmap.json`: `docs/playstation/SECURITY_BOUNDARY.md`. That file did not exist
in `main` at `52f682c8`, and **no test could notice**: `tests/test_architecture.py`'s
`test_deliverables_exist_and_are_substantive` iterates a hand-written list of `docs/architecture/`
names, so a deliverable named in the *data* but living elsewhere was outside every check. The path
appeared once in the whole tree — in `roadmap.json` itself.

Based directly on `main` @ `52f682c8435956c8210b3189cad23ebea973d2de`. **Not** on PR #36:
`git merge-base --is-ancestor aed099d4 HEAD` → non-zero, and the two files PR #36 adds are absent
here. The two PRs can land in either order; neither edits the other's files.

| # | Change | Why |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **`docs/playstation/SECURITY_BOUNDARY.md`** (new, 403 lines) | `M17`'s named deliverable: the analysis, to its four acceptance items |
| 2 | **`tests/test_milestone_deliverables.py`** (new, 4 cases) | Derives required documents from `roadmap.json` itself, so the rule is enforced on the data and not on a copy of it; non-vacuity measured twice |
| 3 | `docs/architecture/roadmap.json` — **one `notes` string on `M17`, state unchanged** | Records that the deliverable is published. `M17` stays `blocked`. `M18`–`M21`, `M9`, `M10` untouched; no acceptance criterion altered |
| 4 | `evidence/m17-security-boundary-v1/` (4 documents + `gen_manifest.py` + `HASHES.txt`) | Pre-implementation scope assessment, falsifier source extracts with retrieval commands, verification transcript, `HASHES.txt` (13 records / 8 distinct paths / 13 OK) |

## The deliverable's findings, briefly

**Method, not vocabulary invention.** The repository already enforces `PUBLIC | INFERRED | UNKNOWN |
RESTRICTED` with `verified | located | not-verified` sources, and `psm/registry.py` rejects anything
else — so the document uses those markers and maps the requested three-way scheme onto them
(`public documentation → PUBLIC`, `observable behaviour →` what was measured here with the command,
`unknown → UNKNOWN`). `RESTRICTED` has no counterpart in the three-way scheme and is **kept**, because
collapsing it into "unknown" would erase the one distinction that governs this milestone.

**A 13-step authentication inventory (S1–S13)**, each row: what must be trusted · who performs it ·
its prerequisite · whether a conventional PC could lawfully provide it (`yes` / `no-anchor` /
`no-input` / `n/a` / `unknown`) · evidence · source class · confidence. No step is described by
mechanism, because for the security device the mechanism is `RESTRICTED` (`C-SEC-01`) and elsewhere
simply not public. The most useful row is the one people get wrong in both directions: a conventional
PC **does** have authenticated boot, measured boot and attestation (UEFI Secure Boot `db`/`dbx`,
AMD PSB authenticating the first firmware block against fused hashes, TPM 2.0 PCRs) — lawful,
documented, ordinary — and **none of it can make Sony's chain accept a PC**, because the anchors are
enrolled by different key holders. Reaching the console's anchor is trust-anchor substitution, which
is §6 of the document, not §2.

**Three feasibility paths, not four.** `BOOT_FEASIBILITY.md` §3 lists A, B, C (`grep -c` on the
heading pattern → 3), and the deliverable restates them by meaning. The count "four" circulated in a
follow-up note about that section was wrong, and is corrected in the audit record rather than
silently.

**All three falsifiers: not observed as of 2026-11-22** — with the size of each finding stated
honestly:

* **F-1** (authorised path to the *inner* components): not observed. Sony publishes the **outer**
  package for update *and* reinstallation on its own support page, so a lawful channel to the file
  exists — which is why this is answered by separating "package" from "inner components" instead of
  hand-waving. Public *claims* of PUP-decryption tooling exist; an unauthorised decryption path is
  §6, not a falsifier.
* **F-2** (full-SoC emulator booting signed software, with published evidence): not observed, **and
  materially closer than the record assumes**. Measured from `api.github.com` here:
  `sharpemu/sharpemu` (★6,692, pushed 2026-11-20) whose own Status says it "can currently load the
  `eboot.bin` of real games, execute native CPU instructions, and partially handle gpu-related
  functionality" and that it ships no copyrighted system firmware; `KytyPS5/KytyPS5` (★12,461,
  pushed 2026-11-21), a "translation layer" needing user-supplied `eboot.bin`/`.zar` dumps;
  `RPCSX/rpcsx` (★2,043, stale since 2026-06-29) with no boot claim in its README. None presents
  security-processor emulation or a boot of the signed system software. So `BOOT_FEASIBILITY`'s
  "publicly unattempted in full" is **stale as worded** — proposed correction in the document's §8.2,
  deliberately not applied to a dated assessment — while its load-bearing qualifier still holds.
  Secondary reports that some project "boots the VSH" are marked `not-verified` and **refused as
  evidence**, per §4's own "with published evidence" bar.
* **F-3** (a Sony-licensed scheme to run the system software on PC): not observed; the reviewed
  material shows the opposite shape (games on PC; streaming from a console).

**Platform-model assessment** in four layers — ordinary PC firmware · a hypothetical PC5 model · the
genuine target · actual authenticated execution — each with what it *can* demonstrate and what it can
never demonstrate, plus a per-step verdict table (`M17`'s item 4). The sentence to keep: **a model
passing its own conformance suite is a statement about the model**, and the roadmap's
`must_not_be_satisfied_by` list (PC5 kernel boot, modelled payload, imitation interface, emulator
menu, screenshot) is inherited unchanged.

**Boundary unchanged, and measured rather than promised.** `tools/`, `psm/`, `kernel/` import no
crypto library; the only occurrences of "decrypt" in `tools/` are refusal sentences
(`tools/firmware.py` 13, 166, 219 — "The PFS image is AES-XTS encrypted; PC5 does not decrypt
it."); `psm/` has no `security` module, and
`tests/test_psm_registry.RegistryRulesTest.test_security_is_restricted_and_has_no_interface` passes.
The document is an engineering and security analysis, not an implementation guide for defeating
authentication, not legal advice, and it proposes nothing that touches a protected artifact.

## Verification

> **Four commits; this body describes the first.** `b1b4580d` → `6b6a7a52` (three sentences in §2: no
> row of the authentication-step table is a capability a conventional PC satisfies end-to-end — the
> finding, not an omission) → `c118e67a3` (two precision fixes where §2.1's prose disagreed with the
> table's own classifications, plus a legend sentence that rows score a step as a whole) →
> **`d09949226c39052fa04827c2c9b440129735a312`** (new §3.1, reconciling the three/four/nine counts of
> the same question across `BOOT_FEASIBILITY.md` §3, `FIRMWARE_ANALYSIS.md` §5 and
> `PS5_SYSTEM_SOFTWARE_TARGET.md` §4, with the blocker's two rows now cited to that nine-row table;
> §8.1 reframed from an arithmetic fix to a citation fix). `HASHES.txt` was regenerated at each step,
> since it records those bytes — its digest in the final tree,
> `0bcc4e7cff108102a8b30a3cf8171f70e68a6b82ad32a7e5afa48530277f3cb9`, equals the commit trailer.
> Every command below was re-run in a **fresh clone of the pushed head**; the figures for the final
> head are in this PR's last comment, together with three self-corrections (a wrong `.pyc` count, a
> manifest digest that had been written rather than measured, and a mis-cited "four paths" that had
> been filed as someone else's error). `M17`–`M21` still `blocked`; no state field moved; nothing here
> is merged, and no merge is requested.

Final tree, in this clone (full transcript in `VERIFICATION-20261122.log`, with every exit code):

```
make docs-check   exit 0   DOCS OK: 71 Markdown files, 34 make targets, links, anchors and commands resolve
make check        exit 0   PASSED: 165 checks, 0 failures · PSM conformance: 261/261
                           CITATIONS OK: 258 · PRESENTATION OK: 13 status rows match roadmap.json · BRAND OK
                           Ran 933 tests in 60.602s · OK (skipped=109)
test_milestone_deliverables  exit 0   Ran 4 tests … OK
test_architecture*.py        exit 0   Ran 53 tests … OK
test_product_identity*.py    exit 0   Ran 19 tests … OK     ← the forbidden-claim scan over every docs/**.md
test_psm*.py                 exit 0   Ran 56 tests … OK
HASHES.txt                   exit 0   13 records, 13 OK, 0 bad
baseline at main 52f682c8:   exit 0   Ran 929 tests in 61.656s · OK (skipped=109) · DOCS OK: 67
```

`933 = 929 + 4`; `71 = 67 + 4` documents; `skipped=109` is the **documented unprovisioned** shape
(no `unicorn` in this sandbox) and is identical to the baseline — nothing here added or removed a
skip. A fresh clone of the pushed head is verified separately and posted as a comment on this PR,
out-of-band, because no file can describe the head that contains it.

**Negative control, measured:** a `git worktree` of `main` at the base commit with only the new test
file copied in → `exit 1`, reporting exactly `[('M17', 'docs/playstation/SECURITY_BOUNDARY.md')]`;
the same suite on this branch → `exit 0`. No repository file was moved, renamed or deleted to
produce it, and the out-of-scope milestones (`M19`'s boot evidence, `M18`'s loader, `M2d`'s
`kernel/usb/`) were **not** reported — the scope property case 4 pins.

**No CI claim:** `actions/workflows` → `total_count: 0`; `ci/build.yml` is tracked in `main` but
deliberately kept outside `.github/workflows/` (see its `ci/README.md`, which is exactly `M1b`'s
blocker). Whatever `gh pr checks` shows for this PR will be reported as it reads.

## Milestone status, stated plainly

**`M17` remains `blocked`. `M18` and `M19` remain `blocked`** (and `M20`, `M21` behind them). The
analysis half is published; the blocker is the absence of a lawful trust path and a lawful input,
not the absence of analysis — a boundary is not crossed by describing it. `M9`/`M10`'s structural
question is left exactly as found.

## Explicitly not in this PR

No change to `tools/`, `boot/`, `kernel/`, `psm/` or the USB code (`git diff --name-only 52f682c8 HEAD
-- tools boot kernel psm src firmware` → empty). No key handling, decryption, signature bypass,
boot-chain circumvention or trust-anchor substitution — specified *or* planned. No Sony binaries,
keys or payload bytes: the repository's `PS5UPDATE.PUP` was analysed only as its 135-byte LFS
pointer (measured: `kind unidentified`, entropy 4.924), and the payload was never fetched. No
physical-hardware or genuine-system-software claim. No USB write, no deployment approval. No merge.
